caveats: Only 4 pair(s); need >= 20 next-trading-day pairs before any RMSE comparison is more than anecdote.
Some pairs span multi-day gaps, so persistence is being asked to hold over a weekend+ rather than one session: 2026-07-11->2026-08-16 (36d), 2026-08-16->2026-09-07 (22d)

Model RMSE is leave-one-pair-out cross-validated, but with 4 pair(s) each fold trains on only 3 pair(s) - the number is out-of-sample but has enormous variance and should not be read as a point estimate. Adjacent pairs also share a snapshot (pair i's t+1 is pair i+1's t), so the folds are not fully independent.

Weekend captures (ET), which carry the prior session's close: #23 (2026-07-11, Sat), #54 (2026-08-16, Sun). calendar_gap_days spans capture timestamps, not trading sessions, so is_next_trading_day can be True for a pair whose market content spans two or more sessions. Exchange holidays are not detected here and have the same effect.
verdict: On 4 pair(s), the model does not beat persistence (model masked RMSE 0.0198 vs persistence 0.0131, relative improvement -51.4%). This is NOT statistically meaningful: too few pairs, some spanning multi-day gaps, and each cross-validation fold trains on almost nothing. Treat it as a pipeline smoke test, not evidence about the model either way.
